key_insight: A real-time $GW$-BSE workflow with localized atom-centered bases and optimized real-space resolution of identity makes accurate optical absorption calculations feasible for systems with thousands of atoms.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the computational barrier for predictive modeling of optoelectronic materials, enabling more practical screening and design of large nanostructures relevant to solar cells and LEDs.
method: Atom-centered basis sets for efficient representation
Locally optimized real-space resolution of the identity
evidence_signal: The method’s per-step cost scales quadratically with system size and the authors demonstrate it by computing the absorption spectrum of a 4616-atom nanographene.
watch_item: While much cheaper than conventional $GW$-BSE, the approach still requires careful implementation and may remain demanding for very large or strongly disordered systems.
paper_title: Optical absorption spectra from the $GW$-Bethe-Salpeter framework for thousands of atoms
